data.description:
Set `merge.ours.driver=true` in the reconciler workflow so the tickets branch's
`.bridge_state/* merge=ours` attribute actually resolves on GHA. Latent bug today; hard prerequisite
for B1. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`init.py:508-511` sets `merge.ours.driver` **per clone**, and it is never committed;
`reconcile-bridge.yml` never sets it. So on the runner the `merge=ours` attribute names an
**undefined driver** and git silently falls back to a 3-way text merge of an **18,231,660-byte** JSON
file — the opposite of the local-wins behaviour the design assumes.

This must land before B1: `blob:none` keeps commits but removes merge-base **blobs**, which the
reconverge path materializes, so filtering while the driver is undefined makes an already-fragile
path lazily fault large blobs mid-merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The reconciler workflow sets `merge.ours.driver=true` for the tickets worktree before any merge
      step. Verify: grep assertion in a workflow lint test.
- [ ] A reconverge against a **diverged** remote in a fresh runner-shaped checkout resolves
      `.bridge_state/*` **local-wins** (not a text merge) and produces no conflict markers. Tier:
      **integration** in a real temporary git repo mimicking the runner setup.
- [ ] The same scenario **without** the config produces the text-merge behaviour — the negative
      control proving the test detects the defect. Tier: **integration**.

## Files
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`, `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`, tests

Scope: XS-S. No dependencies.
data.title: B3: define merge.ours.driver on the reconciler runner (prerequisite for the CI clone filter)
